cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Help me sort our letters before the removal van comes. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. We filled it over ten years. I shouldn't have to decide alone what survives us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose a day we'll open it together. Taking it away can't mean you inherit all the deciding.

mechanism: A directs packing but concedes custody and timing while insisting that decisions about a shared history remain a shared burden.
confusable: Unlike merely getting rid of possessions, A seeks participation because the relationship created the burden; borrowed authority yields logistics to keep joint deciding possible.
comparison: Separating partners and unread letters differ from siblings handling ongoing parent care.
seedUse: Use D77-b letters/removal/box and S02-a revised timetable presented as A decision.
